definition: AirSim (Aerial Informatics and Robotics Simulation) is an open-source, cross-platform simulator for drones, ground vehicles such as cars and various other objects, built on Epic Games’ proprietary Unreal Engine 4 as a platform for AI research.
details: It is developed by Microsoft and can be used to experiment with deep learning, computer vision and reinforcement learning algorithms for autonomous vehicles. This allows testing of autonomous solutions without worrying about real-world damage. AirSim provides some 12 kilometers of roads with 20 city blocks and APIs to retrieve data and control vehicles in a platform independent way. The APIs are accessible via a variety of programming languages, including C++, C#, Python and Java. AirSim supports hardware-in-the-loop with driving wheels and flight controllers such as PX4 for physically and visually realistic simulations. The platform also supports common robotic platforms, such as Robot Operating System (ROS). It is developed as an Unreal plug-in that can be dropped into any Unreal environment. An experimental release for a Unity plug-in is also available. On December 15, 2023 Microsoft has shutdown the development of the project.

explainer.lead: AirSim is a simulator for testing autonomous drones and ground vehicles in realistic virtual environments. It lets researchers train and evaluate AI systems without risking damage to real vehicles or surroundings.

tiers.eli5: AirSim is like a video game where a computer can practise flying a drone or driving a car. If it crashes, nothing in the real world gets broken, so researchers can let it try again and learn. The virtual world runs through Unreal Engine 4, and programs can collect information and steer the vehicles.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers can run AirSim as an Unreal Engine 4 plug-in and use its C++, C#, Python, or Java APIs to retrieve data and control simulated vehicles. It supports ROS and hardware-in-the-loop testing with equipment such as PX4 flight controllers and driving wheels. Microsoft shut down development on December 15, 2023, so teams should account for the project's discontinued status.
tiers.paperLevel: AirSim is an open-source, cross-platform simulation platform for AI research on autonomous drones and ground vehicles. It provides a physically and visually simulated environment, platform-independent vehicle-control and data-retrieval APIs, and interfaces for robotics software and hardware-in-the-loop experiments. Its supplied environment contains about 12 kilometres of roads across 20 city blocks; development was shut down on December 15, 2023.

explainer.example: A researcher testing an autonomous car can run it through AirSim's 20 city blocks, retrieve data through the Python API, and send control commands to the vehicle. A failed manoeuvre can be studied and rerun in simulation without damaging a real car.

explainer.intuition: AirSim replaces the real world with a controllable virtual one, so an autonomous vehicle can sense, act, fail, and be tested repeatedly without causing real-world damage.
howItWorks: Add the AirSim plug-in to an Unreal Engine environment, or use the experimental Unity plug-in.
Place a simulated drone, car, or other supported object in that environment.
Connect an AI or robotics program through AirSim's APIs, ROS, or supported hardware-in-the-loop equipment.
Retrieve simulation data and send vehicle-control commands to run and repeat experiments.
explainer.whyItMatters: AirSim makes autonomous-vehicle experiments safer and repeatable while supporting both AI algorithms and robotics hardware. It also gives researchers a shared simulated setting for deep learning, computer vision, and reinforcement learning work.
misconceptions: AirSim is not an autonomous-driving algorithm; it is a simulator in which algorithms can be tested.
It is not limited to drones, because it also simulates ground vehicles such as cars.
It is not still under active Microsoft development; development was shut down on December 15, 2023.
